newsitem.title: SWEDEN: RESEARCH ALERT-Salomon says Ericsson a buy.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-Salomon says Ericsson a buy.

text.p: Investment bank Salomon Brothers said it had started coverage of Swedish telecoms group Ericsson with a buy recommendation.
But it said it preferred Finnish rival Nokia Oy on a one year view.

"Ericsson's strength in mobile communications and large installed base in the fixed telephone network suggest that the firm will be one of the winners in the current 'golden age' for telecoms equipment suppliers," Salomon Brothers said.
It pointed out that the company has a large installed base in fixed and wireless telecoms.
"Ericsson has the R&D capabilities and financial strength to remain a long-term competitor in this rapidly changing industry," Salomon Brothers said.

It said Ericsson's share price was expensive -- trading six crowns up at 334.5 crowns at 1045 GMT Wednesday -- even considering the correction for Swedish accounting practices that reduced its reported earnings.

"However, its growth potential in wireless infrastructure and handsets, combined with improving performance in the Infocom business area, leads us to expect Ericsson to remain a major growth company well into the 21th century," it said.
It added that on a one-year investment horizon it continued to prefer Nokia.
Relative valuation between Ericsson and Nokia shows Ericsson trading at a significant premium to Nokia based on several ratios.
"At a minimun, we would be forced to conclude that Ericsson is 15 percent more expensive than Nokia," it said.
It concluded that Ericsson's higher R&D investment over the last few years has not made it any more productive than Nokia.
It saw evidence that Ericsson was changing its spending pattern and demanding higher returns on all its investments.
"However, it will take some time before Ericsson's change in policies noticeably affect its profitability," the report said.
"Over the next year, we continue to prefer Nokia over Ericsson as an investment becaues we believe that equity returns are related to returns on total invested capital."
